I can help with that. A washing machine that won't spin usually does so for one of three reasons: it hasn't drained the water yet (it won't spin if there's water inside), the load is unbalanced, or there is a mechanical fault. The most common cause is actually a drainage issue—often just a blocked filter. If the machine can't empty, it will refuse to spin as a safety measure. To narrow this down quickly:
1. Is there still water sitting in the drum?
2. When you start a drain or spin cycle, do you hear the pump humming or running near the bottom of the machine, or is it silent?
no water in the drum, it drained fine. its just the wet mat in there. not sure about the pump noise tbh, the drum tries to speed up then slows down a few times

That 'try to speed up then slow down' pattern usually means one of two things: either the machine is trying to redistribute a load that keeps knocking it off balance (which is normal for a single heavy item like a mat), or there is a drive issue where the motor runs but doesn't turn the drum. To tell them apart quickly, please do this:
1. Take the wet mat out of the machine.
2. Run a spin-only programme with an empty drum.
3. Watch what happens: does it spin up to full speed and stay there, or does it still try to accelerate then slow down? If it spins fine when empty, the issue is just the load balance (a mat often causes this). If it still fails to spin even when empty, we'll need to check the drive belt next.
not sure how to do a spin only on this one tbh, and i havent tried it empty so cant say. is there an easier way to check?

It is often easier than looking for a specific button: just pick any normal cycle (like Cotton 40 or 60), turn the dial to set the Spin speed to 'Max' or 'High', and press Start. Please take the wet mat out first so the drum is empty, then run that cycle. 1. If it spins up to full speed and stays there, the problem was just the mat being unbalanced (this is very common with single heavy items).

ur message cut off after number 2 lol. i havent tried it empty yet tho, whats the 2nd bit?

Apologies for that! The second part was: 2. If it still tries to accelerate then slows down even when empty, the machine likely has a drive fault (such as a worn belt or motor brushes) rather than just an unbalanced load. Since you haven't tried this yet, please take the mat out and run a normal cycle with the drum empty, setting the spin speed to Max. Let me know if it spins up properly when there's nothing inside.
ok but the spin speed is already on 1000, not no spin. i dont really get what u mean by max on this one. does it have to be empty tho? bit of a faff running it with nothing in

You don't need a special 'spin only' button; just pick any normal cycle (like Cotton 40) and ensure the spin speed dial is turned all the way up to its highest number (1000 or similar). It doesn't have to be empty, but testing it empty removes the mat as a variable. If it spins fine when empty, the problem was just the mat being unbalanced (very common with single heavy items like mats).
